strategy.summary: Reproduce scikit-learn non-metric MDS (smacof/MDS) correctness regression covering (1) normalized stress comparison between metric and non-metric, (2) non-metric stress monotonicity over iterations (max_iter=2 vs 3), and (3) stress matching the returned embedding; additionally include the isotonic out-of-bounds numerical path (issue 26999) to trigger NaNs only if the toolchain/version combination matches.

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pip install -r requirements.txt  # if present, else install the versions listed above

pinned_because: evidence constraints: joblib==1.3.1 (non-numerically relevant but included by the instance)
evidence constraints: threadpoolctl==3.2.0 (non-numerically relevant but included by the instance)

the defect involves SMACOF/non-metric stress computation order and normalized Stress-1 behavior, which are numerically sensitive to the BLAS/OpenMP behavior; therefore the instance specifies OpenBLAS via libopenblas and OpenMP True (libgomp)

strategy.test_command: pytest -q sklearn/manifold/tests/test_mds.py -k "nonmetric_lower_normalized_stress or nonmetric_mds_optimization or returned_stress or isotonic_outofbounds"
strategy.reproducing_test: Running the project’s own tests in sklearn/manifold/tests/test_mds.py with the above -k selection. On the buggy revision, at least one of these assertions should fail due to the SMACOF stress/embedding mismatch and/or non-metric stress progression bug; the isotonic out-of-bounds test may raise ValueError('Input contains NaN') on matching numerical conditions.
strategy.success_criterion: Transition at least one selected test from failing on the buggy revision (692289e4939d) to passing on the fixed revision. Concretely: (a) test_nonmetric_mds_optimization should change from FAIL (stress_after_2_iter <= stress_after_3_iter on buggy code, violating the asserted strict decrease from max_iter=2 to 3) to PASS; (b) test_returned_stress should change from FAIL (returned MDS stress_ does not match the stress computed from mds_est.embedding_) to PASS; and optionally (c) test_isotonic_outofbounds should change from FAIL due to NaNs/ValueError to PASS no-error if your environment triggers the same numerical pathology.
strategy.numerical_probe: The probe is the test’s internal computed stress scalar comparisons (not an external print). The key numerical decision points are: for issue 27028 regression, whether stress_ after max_iter=2 is greater than stress_ after max_iter=3 for non-metric; and for issue 16846 regression, whether mds_est.stress_ equals the stress computed from euclidean distances between the returned embedding Z and the original input distances D.

input_output_examples.input: test_nonmetric_lower_normalized_stress: mds.smacof(sim, init=Z, n_components=2, max_iter=1000, n_init=1, normalized_stress=True) vs same call with metric=False, starting from init=Z
input_output_examples.buggy_output: FAIL: assertion assert stress1 > stress2 violated (buggy behavior produces stress2 >= stress1)
input_output_examples.expected_output: PASS: non-metric (metric=False) yields lower normalized stress than metric (metric=True) for this fixed sim/init configuration

input_output_examples.input: test_nonmetric_mds_optimization: load_digits(return_X_y=True), subset size=200 with rng default_rng(seed=42), then fit MDS(metric=False, random_state=42, n_components=2, n_init=1, eps=1e-15, max_iter=2) and max_iter=3; compare mds_est.stress_
input_output_examples.buggy_output: FAIL: assertion assert stress_after_2_iter > stress_after_3_iter violated on buggy revision
input_output_examples.expected_output: PASS: stress decreases when increasing max_iter from 2 to 3 for this non-metric configuration

input_output_examples.input: test_returned_stress: X=[[1,1],[1,4],[1,5],[3,3]]; D=euclidean_distances(X); mds_est=MDS(n_components=2, random_state=42).fit(X); Z=embedding_, stress=stress_; compute stress_Z from euclidean_distances(Z) and compare
input_output_examples.buggy_output: FAIL: assert_allclose(stress, stress_Z) fails (buggy code computes/stores stress at the wrong iteration step vs returned embedding)
input_output_examples.expected_output: PASS: returned mds_est.stress_ matches stress_Z computed from returned embedding distances

input_output_examples.input: test_isotonic_outofbounds: dis and init fixed arrays; call mds.smacof(dis, init=init, metric=False, n_init=1)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: FAIL or ERROR on buggy revision on matching numerical conditions: ValueError('Input contains NaN') arising from euclidean_distances(check_array) within the non-metric path (issue 26999)

risks: The exact failing test(s) depend on the fixed commit content; the evidence provides the buggy commit SHA (692289e4939d) but not the fixed commit SHA. Substitute once known so the buggy->fixed transition is real.

The isotonic_outofbounds/NaN failure (issue 26999 symptom) may be sensitive to BLAS/OpenMP builds and CPU/architecture. The instance specifies OpenBLAS via libopenblas and OpenMP True (libgomp) and that threadpoolctl reports OpenBLAS; if your runner differs, test_isotonic_outofbounds may pass on both revisions (still OK if the other assertions fail).

Non-determinism risk: the tests that select digits subset use rng.default_rng(seed=42) and pass random_state=42 into MDS; keep determinism by not changing NumPy/BLAS threading env vars during the test run (or keep them consistent across buggy/fixed runs).

If the environment uses a different Python/NumPy/SciPy ABI than specified, numerical comparisons like assert stress_after_2_iter > stress_after_3_iter may not reproduce reliably; keep the pinned versions from the instance.

OpenBLAS/OpenMP implementation details are part of the documented dependency constraint in the instance (“numerical_backend: OpenBLAS via libopenblas; OpenMP built with OpenMP True (libgomp)”). If your environment uses MKL or different OpenMP runtime, the NaN/monotonicity manifestation may change.

oracle.reference_source: The reproduction is the project’s own unit tests in sklearn/manifold/tests/test_mds.py (the asserts define the oracle).
oracle.why: The provided evidence includes wrong-value/exception symptoms, but not an external numeric reference. The selected tests directly encode expected inequalities and equality with stress computed from the returned embedding, which is sufficient for FAIL/PASS transition.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On revision 692289e4939d, expected FAIL at least for test_nonmetric_mds_optimization and/or test_returned_stress: (1) stress computed/stored corresponds to the wrong iteration step so stress_after_2_iter can be <= stress_after_3_iter; and/or (2) stress_ does not correspond to the returned embedding, so stress_Z (computed from returned embedding Z) disagrees with mds_est.stress_. Additionally, depending on numerical conditions, test_isotonic_outofbounds may raise ValueError: Input contains NaN.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision corresponding to PR #30514, expected PASS for the same tests: stress is computed from the correct embedding (so test_returned_stress passes) and non-metric normalized stress / iteration monotonicity assertions hold (so test_nonmetric_lower_normalized_stress and test_nonmetric_mds_optimization pass).
